import FormalConjecturesUtil
/-!
# Erdős Problem 1139

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1139](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1139)
-/

open Nat Filter
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.Omega
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1139

/--
Let $1\leq u_1 < u_2 < \cdots$ be the sequence of integers with at most $2$ prime factors.
Is it true that $$\limsup_{k \to \infty} \frac{u_{k+1}-u_k}{\log k}=\infty?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1139 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      letI u := Nat.nth (fun n ↦ 0 < n ∧ Ω n ≤ 2)
      atTop.limsup (fun k : ℕ ↦ (((u (k + 1) : ℝ) - (u k : ℝ)) / Real.log (↑k + 1) : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos1139

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a zero-indexed enumeration with denominator log(k + 1), and expresses the infinite upper limit as an EReal limsup equal to ⊤.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The predicate 0 < n ∧ Ω n ≤ 2 is infinite because it contains every prime. Thus Nat.nth genuinely enumerates it in increasing order. Writing the source's one-indexed sequence as U_j = u(j − 1), the Lean ratio at k is exactly the source ratio at j = k + 1. This shift preserves limsup. The k = 0 quotient is zero under Lean's division convention, but this single initial value is irrelevant. Finite-input EReal arithmetic agrees with real arithmetic, and EReal limsup = ⊤ is equivalent to exceeding every real bound somewhere in every tail. Both the reindexing equivalence and this limsup characterization were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
